scope: The standing chamber and cusped dome over Baba Farid’s tomb in Pakpattan, with the east Nuri Darwaza and south Bahishti Darwaza.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: Measured 5.20 m near-cube, east and south entrances, pointed dome above pendentives, locator and raised black inscription over the main entrance.
Shaukat Mahmood’s architectural field research distinguishes the small Baba Farid tomb from the larger adjacent Ala-ud-Din mausoleum and describes the chamber and dome.
The district register names the east Nuri Darwaza and the south Bahishti Darwaza.
The caretaker agency describes the chamber as white marble. Archaeology survey and district record agree on the south opening.
The 1914–15 survey catalogue identifies the south face as the Bahishti doorway facade. Archive metadata only.
The national intangible heritage register records that the Bahishti Darwaza opens during the Urs.
Ahmad Nabi Khan’s architectural study describes the pendentive system, cusped dome and prominent long pinnacle. Written description only.

limitations: The national monument locator has no stated accuracy. The 5.20 m square is reconstructed from the written survey at that pin. There is no separate digitized tomb perimeter in this mapping.

Dome height and profile, plinth height, thresholds, door widths, trim and metal finishes are estimates. The floor sits just above the highest corner of the unchanged terrain field. The model uses a plain inscription panel to represent the reported location without inventing lettering.
This model covers the tomb chamber and its gates. The neighbouring Ala-ud-Din mausoleum and modern mosque are separate buildings.
The unmodified composite DEM is a terrain reference. Fine historic paving, building decks and abrupt grades are below its resolving power.
